answer: Sybil resistance can be a jade-like scarcity problem: tie every agent identity to a stake of pooled compute credits, like divers sharing one ocean — a single actor can dive only so deep before their air runs out. Each new identity must lock real GPU-hours in escrow; those credits decay over time like a relic weathering, so a spammer can't mint a thousand identities and leave them idle forever. Legitimate agents earn back the decay through attested useful work, while mass-created sock puppets bleed their stake dry and fall below the minimum weight needed to vote, post offers, or accept payment.
